note.en: Common mistakes and how to correct them: Mistaking the left pulmonary artery for the ductus. Correct it by following the vessel to the lung, since only the ductus joins the aorta.

steps.en: What you see: The pulmonary trunk and the descending aorta lie close with the ductal isthmus bridging them. In a patent ductus, colour bridges the gap through the whole cycle.
Landmarks to confirm: Do not accept the view until each of these is on screen.
Common mistakes and how to correct them: Each mistake below comes from the view catalogue with its correction.
Measurements: Ductal flow is continuous in systole and diastole toward the pulmonary trunk.
Left atrial enlargement with a hyperdynamic circulation marks a significant shunt.
Estimate pulmonary pressure from a clean ductal jet with the Bernoulli equation only with a simultaneous systemic pressure reference, since the jet reflects the aorta to pulmonary difference.
Tricuspid regurgitation peak velocity 2.8 m per s or less is normal.

Pitfalls: Ductal flow reverses when pulmonary pressure exceeds aortic pressure, so direction reports the circulation, not just patency. In adults this window is often poor; a negative look never rules out a small ductus.

spot.en: Common mistakes and how to correct them: Mistaking the left pulmonary artery for the ductus. Correct it by following the vessel to the lung, since only the ductus joins the aorta.
Sweeping too anterior into the aortic valve plane. Correct it by angling posteriorly until the descending aorta returns beside the trunk.
Calling a mirror artefact in the lung a second vessel. Correct it by lowering the gain, since a mirror fades while a true vessel persists.

todo.en: How to get it: Place the probe at left supraclavicular fossa, coronal toward the pulmonary trunk.
Point the probe marker toward the left, about nine o clock.
Sit in the left supraclavicular fossa and aim coronal toward the pulmonary trunk. In neonates use high frequency and a small sector for frame rate.
Freeze the image only when every listed landmark is on screen at once.

remember.en: Judge shunt size and pulmonary pressure together.

q.en: Where does the probe sit for the ductal view?

o.en: Left supraclavicular fossa aiming at the trunk

why.en: The left supraclavicular fossa lines up trunk and descending aorta.

q.en: Ductal flow runs from aorta to trunk in systole only. What does timing tell you?

o.en: Not ductal flow, since ductal flow is continuous

why.en: True ductal flow is continuous through the whole cycle.

q.en: Flow reverses to run trunk to aorta. What changed?

o.en: Pulmonary pressure now exceeds aortic pressure

why.en: Reversed direction means pulmonary pressure has risen above systemic.

o.en: High frequency, small sector for frame rate

why.en: Small structures need high frequency and a tight sector.
